VI-M1.title: Reference rejects when L1 card_id differs from payment_instrument.id
VI-M1.reference: verification/chain.py step '4c-bis' (commented 'Optional card_id cross-check (SHOULD-level)') returns an error whenever L1 carries card_id and it differs from the mandate's payment_instrument.id.
VI-M1.spec: credential-format.md §3.3: card_id is OPTIONAL, an 'Opaque card-level identifier assigned by the Issuer'; payment_instrument.id is an 'Instrument instance identifier (e.g., a token UUID)' (§4.4.2). No section requires them to be equal, and the spec's own examples use card_id 'card-mc-8842' (§3.6) with payment_instrument.id 'f199c3dd-…' (§11).
VI-M1.assessment: KYA follows the text. The reference enforces an unwritten binding as a hard failure despite its own 'SHOULD-level' comment. Not a KYA bug; candidate note for the VI Issue.

TAP-M1.title: Reference only reads the camel-case keyId parameter
TAP-M1.reference: cdn-proxy/server.js parseRFC9421SignatureInput returns attributes.keyId; with RFC 9421 'keyid' it is undefined, validateKeyId fails and the request is rejected with 'Invalid Key ID Format' before any other check.
TAP-M1.spec: RFC 9421 §2.3 and the Visa merchant specification page use 'keyid'; RFC 8941 keys are lower-case only. The repo's own merchant-backend verifier also expects 'keyid'. See spec gap TAP-02.
TAP-M1.assessment: KYA follows RFC 9421 and the Visa page; the reference proxy and agent agree with each other but not with either. Every RFC-spelled TAP vector is rejected for this one reason, so TAP agreements on reject vectors are incidental.

TAP-M2.title: Reference accepts the keyId spelling that KYA leaves undefined
TAP-M2.reference: The reference agent emits keyId and the proxy accepts it.
TAP-M2.spec: Spec gap TAP-02: repo (keyId) vs RFC 9421 / Visa page (keyid).
TAP-M2.assessment: Expected: the reference resolves the gap in favour of its own spelling. Confirms TAP-02 is a real interoperability split rather than a theoretical one.

AP2-M1.title: SDK verifies a checkout mandate presented without a payment mandate
AP2-M1.reference: MandateClient.verify works per chain; the adapter (like the merchant sample) verifies whatever chains are presented.
AP2-M1.spec: specification.md Modes: 'Verifiers of Mandates always receive a closed Payment and Checkout Mandate, regardless of the mode.' Verification rules are per role (Merchant: checkout; Credential Provider/Network: payment).
AP2-M1.assessment: Both readings are defensible: KYA, as a neutral whole-transaction verifier, applies the 'always receive both' sentence; a single-role verifier legitimately sees one chain. Recorded as a scoping difference, not a bug on either side.

AP2-G.title: SDK decides cases KYA leaves undefined
AP2-G.reference: AP2-01 cart total vs amount: not compared (accept). AP2-02 mixed flows: accept. AP2-04 decimal max 250.0: treated as minor units (reject). AP2-05 recurrence period: SDK's own period arithmetic (accept). AP2-06 budget: major units, max x 100 (accept). AP2-07 'product' line items: UCP schema validation fails (reject). AP2-08 no revealed acceptable_items: wildcard (accept).
AP2-G.spec: See docs/spec-gaps.md AP2-01..AP2-08: in each case the docs are silent or contradict the schema/SDK.
AP2-G.assessment: These are the reference's choices where the text does not decide. AP2-04 and AP2-06 together show the unit problem: the SDK reads amount_range.max as minor units but budget.max as major units.

AP2-O1.title: Observation: the SDK's checkout chain does not recompute checkout_hash on its own
AP2-O1.reference: CheckoutMandateChain.verify compares checkout_hash only with a caller-supplied expected_checkout_hash; ap2-checkout-hash-mismatch is rejected through the payment chain's transaction_id comparison instead.
AP2-O1.spec: specification.md Merchant verification: 'Verify that the hash of the Checkout JWT sent for approval matches the value included for the checkout_hash claim.'
AP2-O1.assessment: Same verdict here, but a merchant that verifies only the checkout chain must recompute the hash itself. Not a divergence; noted for implementers.

VI-G.title: Spec-gap vectors masked by the card_id check
VI-G.reference: Rejected by VI-M1 before the gap-relevant logic runs.
VI-G.assessment: No information about the reference's handling of these gaps; recorded for completeness.

TAP-G.title: Spec-gap vectors masked by the keyId check
TAP-G.reference: Rejected by TAP-M1 before tag or payment-container handling.
TAP-G.spec: TAP-01, TAP-03. The reference implements neither the payment container nor a tag/operation check.
